title: High concurrency scenario (199 to 999 users and cache stampede)
hook: When traffic jumps from 199 to 999 concurrent users, a cold Redis key can trigger a cache stampede — hundreds of threads miss cache and hammer the database at once. Fix it with single-flight loading, semaphores, and never holding locks across I/O.

blocks.text: A cache stampede happens when many parallel requests discover the same cache miss and all load the backing store simultaneously. Single-flight (also called request coalescing) ensures only one loader runs per key while others await the same Task. SemaphoreSlim limits outbound database connections. Combine with async I/O (module 13), allocation awareness (module 14), and concurrent collections from this module.

entries.plainDefinition: Many clients miss cache at once and overload the origin data source.
entries.example: 999 users request profile/42 when Redis key expired.

entries.plainDefinition: Deduplicate in-flight loads so one fetch satisfies many waiters.
entries.example: ConcurrentDictionary<string, Task<User>> tracks ongoing loads per key.

entries.plainDefinition: Many workers wake or proceed at once after a shared event.
entries.example: All threads pass cache miss check before any sets Redis.

blocks.text: This is a classic senior interview scenario tying async, locking, caching, and LINQ deferred execution together. Wrong fixes — global lock around Redis get and DB query — serialize all keys and destroy throughput. Right fixes — per-key single-flight, short-lived in-memory gate, Redis SET NX, or stale-while-revalidate.

blocks.title: Interview story arc
blocks.body: Describe the spike, measure DB connection count, implement single-flight with ConcurrentDictionary of Task, add SemaphoreSlim on DB pool, verify allocation rate did not spike from ToList on hot path.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Detect stampede
items.body: Redis miss rate and DB connection count spike together.

items.title: Coalesce per key
items.body: First miss starts Task; subsequent misses await same Task.

items.title: Limit DB fan-out
items.body: SemaphoreSlim caps concurrent queries even across keys.

items.title: Warm or stagger expiry
items.body: Jitter TTL; background refresh before expiry.

diagram.title: Single-flight cache load
diagram.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant R1 as Request 1
  participant R2 as Request 2
  participant SF as Single-flight
  participant DB as Database
  R1->>SF: miss key K
  SF->>DB: start load K
  R2->>SF: miss key K
  SF-->>R2: await same Task
  DB-->>SF: result
  SF-->>R1: result
  SF-->>R2: result

snippet.label: Single-flight with ConcurrentDictionary
snippet.explanation: GetOrAdd ensures one LoadAndCacheAsync per id at a time. Others await the shared Task.

snippet.label: DB throttle semaphore
snippet.explanation: Even with single-flight per key, many keys can still hit DB — cap total concurrent queries.

snippet.label: Anti-pattern: lock across Redis
snippet.explanation: Global lock plus blocking I/O destroys concurrency. Never hold locks across network calls.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Global lock on cache path. Forgetting to remove completed entries from _inflight — memory leak of Task references. Materializing entire user list with LINQ ToList on every miss. Ignoring CancellationToken when coalesced waiters cancel.

interviewTakeaways: Cache stampede: many parallel misses overload the origin.
Single-flight coalesces in-flight loads per key.
Never lock across Redis, HTTP, or database I/O.
commonPitfalls: Global lock around cache and DB.
No semaphore on total DB concurrency.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Storing Map<string, Promise<T>> for in-flight loads is the same single-flight pattern as ConcurrentDictionary<string, Task<T>>.
